solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Better gets on convenient-sounding race

definitions.note: a handicap is a race in which runners are weighted to even their chances

indicators.note: the hyphenated -sounding tells us only the sound of the word for convenient is wanted

parts.note: convenient means handy
to better is to cap, as in capping someone's story

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse in a race whose name sounds handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as a gambler, but it is the verb meaning to outdo; 'gets on' puts it after the sound of HANDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a horse race where weights are assigned to equalise the field.

clue.text: Here skiing challenge has an extra round

indicators.note: round says the letters for an extra go around the word for challenge

parts.note: an gives A
extra means more
to challenge or compete is to vie

explanation.surface: A ski slope's challenge comes with a bonus round.
explanation.walkthrough: AVIEMORE is a ski resort in the Scottish Highlands, in the Cairngorms.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviemore is Britain's best-known winter sports resort, the place to go skiing in Scotland.

clue.text: Work on New Year list and act as host

parts.note: to do something is to work on it, as in doing the garden
the New Year Honours is the list of British awards announced on 1 January

explanation.surface: Someone labours over the New Year Honours list and plays host.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Year Honours is the UK list of knighthoods and medals published each January.
explanation.definitionFit: To do the honours is an idiom for serving guests, pouring drinks or carving as the host.

clue.text: Mike comes in to devise a tasty indulgence

indicators.note: comes in signals that the letter for Mike is placed inside the rest

parts.note: to devise is to create
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Mike invents a delicious treat.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of scones with clotted cream, jam and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones heaped with clotted cream and jam make a rich treat, an indulgence rather than a meal.

clue.text: How long Dad took to complete crosswords, for example

parts.note: Dad's is PA'S, the possessive of pa
how long something took is its time

explanation.surface: Someone asks how long their father took over the crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How long Dad took' reads as PA'S TIME, the time belonging to Dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Solving crosswords is a classic leisure hobby, one example of a way to pass the hours.

clue.text: Potentially Iron Age bird?

parts.note: pig iron is crude metal that can be refined into iron, so pig is potentially iron
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: Was some bird around in the Iron Age?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Age' looks like one historical period, but it splits: pig before iron, eon for age.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common bird of the dove family.

clue.text: No end of bother over one mystic

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the letters are turned upwards, read in reverse
No end of means the last letter of the word for bother is dropped

parts.note: bother means fuss
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Endless trouble falls on one mystic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'endless', but it cuts the final S of FUSS; 'over' then turns FUS into SUF.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is a follower of the mystical branch of Islam.

clue.text: Emblem carried by revolutionary was continually annoying

indicators.note: carried by puts the emblem on top of the revolutionary, which in a down light means before it

parts.note: an emblem is a badge
a revolutionary is a Red, a communist

explanation.surface: A revolutionary wearing a badge kept pestering people.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger is to pester persistently, as a dog harries a badger.

clue.text: A very important fact about unusual native animals: just tips for birds

indicators.note: just tips means only the first letter of each of the eight words is used

explanation.surface: A naturalist's key fact about strange native creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word; everything before 'just tips' supplies one initial letter per word.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the collective term for the bird life of a region.

clue.text: Make a picture, forswearing a beer

indicators.note: forswearing means giving up, so the second a is dropped from the word for making a picture

parts.note: to paint is to make a picture

explanation.surface: An artist gives up painting to have a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is the standard serving of beer in a British pub.

clue.text: To try going viral is tragic

parts.note: a judge hears a case, that is tries it
content going viral online is trending

explanation.surface: Desperately trying to go viral is a sad business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To try' looks like attempting, but it is the legal sense, as a court tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-rending is so sad it breaks the heart, as a tragedy does.

clue.text: Clamour to play with Haydn, in this state?

indicators.note: to play suggests letters being toyed with and set in new order

explanation.surface: A noisy crowd demands that Haydn be performed.
explanation.walkthrough: Haydn served the Habsburgs; the clue nods to Austria-Hungary, the best-known dual monarchy, though it formed after his death.
explanation.definitionFit: A dual monarchy is a political union of two kingdoms under a single ruler, a kind of state.

clue.text: I don't care if this protects pig from sunburn?

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
the thing that protects from sunburn is a hat

explanation.surface: A farmer shrugs off whether a hat would shield a pig from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pictures a sow wearing a sun hat; the two words together are a shrugging reply.
explanation.definitionFit: So what is a dismissive retort meaning the speaker is indifferent.

clue.text: Perhaps tiger at first makes no time for aardvark

definitions.note: a tiger is one example, signalled by perhaps

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of makes and also places it at the front

parts.note: first letter of makes

indicators.note: no time means a T is removed from the animal's name

parts.note: the aardvark is also called the African anteater

explanation.surface: A tiger spares no time before making a meal of an aardvark.
explanation.walkthrough: The aardvark is also known as the African anteater, which a solver needs to know before taking out the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Some tigers become notorious for attacking people, the classic example of a man-eater.

clue.text: To put on head, secure large cushion

indicators.note: To put on places the word for secure after the word for head

parts.note: bean is slang for head
to bag something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a cushion on their head and fasten it.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanbag is a big floppy seat or cushion filled with polystyrene beads.

clue.text: Reserve weapon: it can reduce work for members?

definitions.text: it can reduce work for members?

parts.note: to reserve is to book
a club is a weapon

explanation.surface: A spare weapon is offered as a labour-saving device for a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is a literary work and 'reduce' means sell at a discount.
explanation.definitionFit: Book clubs offered members novels at cut prices, so a book is a work sold cheaper to members.

clue.text: Inclined to take too much, admitting scarcity not ended

indicators.note: admitting means letting the rest in, so the overdose letters hold the others

parts.note: to OD is to overdose

indicators.note: not ended means the final letter of the scarcity word is removed

parts.note: a famine is a scarcity of food

explanation.surface: Someone prone to excess admits food is short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take too much' reads as part of the definition, but it is the verb OD, short for overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of a mind to do something is to be disposed or minded to do it.

clue.text: Copper abandoned remote obsession

parts.note: remote means far
to have a thing about something is to be obsessed by it

explanation.surface: A police officer gives up a far-fetched fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a police officer, but here it is a copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was a small British bronze coin worth a quarter penny, withdrawn in 1961.

clue.text: Stretch of land without a green? Keep out of it

parts.note: no as in no money means without
a green light means go
a stretch of land is an area

explanation.surface: A landowner warns off visitors from a plot without a golf green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like a golf or village green; it is the traffic light meaning go.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go area is a district barred to outsiders, a place one is told to avoid.

clue.text: Kept short socks, initially coloured

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of socks

parts.note: coloured means tinted

explanation.surface: A short supply of socks was dyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinted means restricted in supply, given a meagre allowance.

clue.text: Holder transferred from can to cup

indicators.note: transferred means the letters are shifted about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drink is poured from a can into a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is only a link; the fodder is the three words 'can to cup'.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant holds a position or property, so is its holder.

clue.text: In surprise attack start to beat into a pulp

indicators.note: into places the first letter of beat inside the other letters

parts.note: mush is a soft pulp

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of beat

explanation.surface: An assailant begins to pound someone into a pulp in an ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is an attack from hiding on unsuspecting victims.

clue.text: Renounce somewhat degenerate backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the run of letters is read the other way
somewhat means only part of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Someone disowns a degenerate cause they had supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for something degenerate; it reverses EGENER found inside 'degenerate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or abandon a commitment.

clue.text: Independent voter annoyed by crazy Bren toting revolutionary

parts.note: annoyed means cross

indicators.note: toting means carrying, so the shuffled gun name carries the revolutionary inside it
crazy says the letters of the gun name are jumbled

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: An angry independent politician is armed with a Bren gun and a guerrilla.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bren is a British light machine gun; Che is Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: In the House of Lords crossbenchers sit apart from the parties, voting independently.

clue.text: Make contact with skin, scraping the top: the reaction?

indicators.note: scraping the top removes the first letter, the top in a down clue

parts.note: to touch is to make contact with the skin

explanation.surface: Someone touches skin, grazes the surface and yelps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation of pain someone utters on getting a graze.

clue.text: Choose either end of coiled string

indicators.note: Choose asks for a pick between the two end letters, so the word for that choice sits between them
end of, with either, picks both the first and last letters of coiled as alternatives

parts.note: either goes with or: one end or the other

explanation.surface: Pick up either end of a coil of string.
explanation.walkthrough: Choosing between the ends of 'coiled' is C OR D, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cord is thin rope or thick twine, a kind of string.

clue.text: Immoral relative has time for a bit of lunch

indicators.note: for means the new letters stand in place of the removed one

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: a bit of takes the first letter of lunch

explanation.surface: A relative takes time out for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of UNCLE, the first bit of lunch, is swapped for HAS plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchaste means not sexually virtuous, hence loose or immoral.

clue.text: Food here may be taken back to the lab

definitions.text: Food here may be taken back to the lab

parts.words: Food here may be taken back to the lab
parts.note: leftovers are carried home from a restaurant ostensibly for the dog, here a Labrador

explanation.walkthrough: 'lab' suggests a laboratory and samples; it is a Labrador, the dog the leftovers are notionally for.
explanation.definitionFit: A doggy bag holds restaurant leftovers that a diner takes home, supposedly for the pet.
